## Paris Apartment Rental Checklist for a 12-Month Lease
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

A practical pre-move checklist for a **12-month unfurnished or furnished lease** in Paris starting **2026-09-01**, tailored for someone relocating from outside France. I’m assuming you want a standard private rental in Paris proper, not student housing or a corporate lease.

## What to Prepare Before You Apply
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg

- **Identity**
  - Passport
  - Visa / residence permit if already issued
  - If applicable: French ID or residence card for co-signers

- **Proof of income**
  - Last 3 payslips, if employed
  - Employment contract or offer letter
  - Last 1–3 tax returns
  - Bank statements showing stable funds
  - If self-employed: company registration, recent accounts, tax filings

- **Proof of address**
  - Recent utility bill, lease, or official letter from your current country
  - If you have no French address yet, a clear explanation and overseas address

- **Guarantor documents**
  - Many Paris landlords want a **French guarantor**
  - If you do not have one, ask whether they accept **bank guarantee**, **insurance-backed guarantor services**, or **corporate relocation support**

- **Rental file extras**
  - Short cover note introducing yourself, move-in date, job status, and why you are a reliable tenant
  - Translation of key documents into French if the originals are not in French or English
  - Digital and PDF copies ready to send quickly

## Costs and Fees to Budget For
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-euro.svg

- **Security deposit**
  - Usually **1 month’s rent** for unfurnished leases
  - Often up to **2 months’ rent** for furnished leases

- **Agency fee**
  - If you use an agent, expect a fee for tenant services; in Paris this is usually capped by law and depends on the apartment size and location
  - Ask exactly who pays what before viewing

- **First month’s rent**
  - Typically paid before move-in, sometimes pro-rated if you move in mid-month

- **Inventory / check-in inspection fee**
  - May be charged or shared depending on the setup
  - Make sure the move-in condition report is detailed

- **Utilities**
  - Electricity, internet, and sometimes gas are usually separate
  - Water may be included or billed separately depending on the building

- **Insurance**
  - Tenant liability insurance is commonly required before key handover

- **Other possible costs**
  - Moving company or van
  - Translation / notarization of documents
  - Bank transfer fees if paying from abroad
  - Temporary accommodation if the lease starts before your arrival

## Questions to Ask the Landlord or Agent
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/chat-square-text.svg

- Is the lease **furnished or unfurnished**, and what exactly is included?
- What is the **monthly rent**, and what charges are included in the “charges” amount?
- What is the **total move-in cost**: deposit, first rent, agency fee, and any other charges?
- Is the apartment **eligible for a 12-month lease** and what is the exact lease start date?
- What is the **notice period** for ending the lease?
- Is there a **French guarantor requirement**, and are alternatives accepted?
- Are **utilities** already connected, or do I need to set them up?
- Is there **internet access**, and which providers serve the building?
- What is the **heating system** and estimated winter cost?
- How is **maintenance** handled for repairs, appliances, and plumbing issues?
- Are there any **building rules** about guests, noise, bikes, trash, or pets?
- Can I see the **energy rating** and recent utility estimates?
- Will I receive a **proper written lease**, inventory report, and rent receipt?

## Red Flags to Watch For
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg

- The landlord asks for **cash only** or pressures you to pay before seeing the lease
- The listing price is **far below market** for the area
- You are asked to send money to a **personal account** with no contract
- The landlord refuses to provide a **written lease** or inventory report
- The apartment is shown with **no access for viewing** or only through vague excuses
- The person claims to be abroad and wants a fast transfer to “hold” the flat
- The deposit or fees seem unusually high or unclear
- The apartment lacks basic legal details such as address, floor area, or landlord identity
- Photos look copied, inconsistent, or do not match the address
- The landlord won’t confirm whether the building has **heating, hot water, or working appliances**
- You are told to sign immediately without time to review the contract

## Move-In Checklist for the First Week
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar-check.svg

- Sign the lease only after reading the rent, charges, deposit, notice period, and repair clauses
- Complete the **entry inventory** carefully and photograph every room, appliance, wall, floor, window, and meter
- Set up **tenant insurance** before key handover if required
- Register electricity, gas, and internet if they are not already active
- Save copies of the lease, inventory, payment receipts, and landlord contact details
- Confirm how rent is paid each month and when receipts will be issued
